name: Ramo Maharana
description: LACMA credits Ramo Maharana alongside Panu Maharana for Krishna’s Dance of Delight (Rasa Lila), dated 1952. The museum record is the source for this attribution.

name: Panu Maharana
description: LACMA credits Panu Maharana alongside Ramo Maharana for Krishna’s Dance of Delight (Rasa Lila), dated 1952. The museum record is the source for this attribution.

name: Ganga Devi
description: Mithila artist Ganga Devi is associated with kachni linework and paintings that include traditional subjects alongside personal experiences. Smarthistory discusses the range of her work and the tradition's social context.

name: Durga Bai Vyam
description: Durga Bai Vyam is an artist whose work includes folktales and images rooted in her Gond Pardhan community. IGNCA describes the role of family, childhood painting and storytelling in her practice.

name: Jivya Soma Mashe
description: Jivya Soma Mashe was an artist from the Warli community whose works are represented in the Fondation Cartier collection and the Fukuoka Asian Art Museum. Explore an individual work through the museum record to see his name attached to a particular painting.

name: Theertham Balaji
description: In a 2010 interview, Srikalahasti artist Theertham Balaji described training under S. Rambhoji Naik, working mainly in natural dyes on cotton, and painting village life as well as religious subjects.

name: A. S. Wungmareo Khaiyar
description: The National Institute of Fashion Technology profiles A. S. Wungmareo Khaiyar of Nungbi Khullen, an artisan who makes hand-moulded pottery including bowls, kettles and cups.

name: Machihan Sasa
description: The Government of India’s Padma Awards citation describes Machihan Sasa’s work in Longpi blackstone pottery and his role in expanding the range of forms made.

name: Sufiyan Ismail Khatri
description: The Museum of International Folk Art credits Sufiyan Ismail Khatri with the Ajrakh block-printed base of a silk scarf also embroidered by Asif Shaikh.

name: Asif Shaikh
description: The Museum of International Folk Art credits Asif Shaikh with the embroidery on a scarf block-printed by Sufiyan Ismail Khatri.

name: Prakash Joshi
description: The Crafts Museum credits Prakash Joshi of Bhilwara, Rajasthan, with the Phad-inspired painting on its entrance gate.
